audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Peter text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for living stones, royal priesthood, honorable conduct, civic order, enslaved household passage with anti-abuse and anti-slavery safeguards, Messiah's suffering.

verses.restored: Therefore putting away all harmfulness and all deceit and hypocrisies and envies and all slanders,

familiar.text: Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings,

modern.text: Rid yourselves, therefore, of all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander.

original.text: Ἀποθέμενοι οὖν πᾶσαν κακίαν καὶ πάντα δόλον καὶ ⸀ὑποκρίσεις καὶ φθόνους καὶ πάσας καταλαλιάς,

verses.restored: as newborn infants, long for the unmixed milk of the word, so that by it you may grow into salvation/healing,

familiar.text: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:

modern.text: Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up in your salvation,

original.text: ὡς ἀρτιγέννητα βρέφη τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα ἐπιποθήσατε, ἵνα ἐν αὐτῷ αὐξηθῆτε ⸂εἰς σωτηρίαν⸃,

verses.restored: if indeed you tasted that the Lord is kind.

familiar.text: If so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.

modern.text: now that you have tasted that the Lord is good.

original.text: ⸀εἰ ἐγεύσασθε ὅτι χρηστὸς ὁ κύριος.

verses.restored: Coming to him, a living stone, rejected by humans but chosen and precious before the Divine,

familiar.text: To whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious,

modern.text: As you come to Him, the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight,

original.text: Πρὸς ὃν προσερχόμενοι, λίθον ζῶντα, ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων μὲν ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον παρὰ δὲ θεῷ ἐκλεκτὸν ἔντιμον

verses.restored: you yourselves also, as living stones, are being built as spiritual house, into holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to the Divine through Jesus Messiah.

familiar.text: Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.

modern.text: you also, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

original.text: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε οἶκος πνευματικὸς ⸀εἰς ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον, ἀνενέγκαι πνευματικὰς θυσίας ⸀εὐπροσδέκτους θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ·

verses.restored: Because it stands in Scripture: Look, I place in Zion a stone, chosen, precious cornerstone, and the one trusting upon him will certainly not be put to shame.

familiar.text: Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.

modern.text: For it stands in Scripture: “See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”

original.text: διότι περιέχει ⸀ἐν γραφῇ· Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον ⸂ἀκρογωνιαῖον ἐκλεκτὸν⸃ ἔντιμον, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ.

verses.restored: Therefore the honor is for you who trust, but for those who do not trust, the stone that the builders rejected, this became head of corner,

familiar.text: Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner,

modern.text: To you who believe, then, this stone is precious. But to those who do not believe, “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,”

original.text: ὑμῖν οὖν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν· ⸀ἀπιστοῦσιν δὲ ⸀λίθος ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας

verses.restored: and a stone of stumbling and rock of offense; they stumble by disobeying the word, into which also they were appointed.

familiar.text: And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.

modern.text: and, “A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble because they disobey the word—and to this they were appointed.

original.text: καὶ λίθος προσκόμματος καὶ πέτρα σκανδάλου· οἳ προσκόπτουσιν τῷ λόγῳ ἀπειθοῦντες· εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐτέθησαν.

verses.restored: But you are chosen lineage, royal priesthood, holy nation, people for possession, so that you may proclaim the excellencies of the One calling you out of darkness into his marvelous light.

familiar.text: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:

modern.text: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.

original.text: Ὑμεῖς δὲ γένος ἐκλεκτόν, βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα, ἔθνος ἅγιον, λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν, ὅπως τὰς ἀρετὰς ἐξαγγείλητε τοῦ ἐκ σκότους ὑμᾶς καλέσαντος εἰς τὸ θαυμαστὸν αὐτοῦ φῶς·

verses.restored: Once not a people, but now people of Divine; once not having received mercy, but now having received mercy.

familiar.text: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.

modern.text: Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.

original.text: οἵ ποτε οὐ λαὸς νῦν δὲ λαὸς θεοῦ, οἱ οὐκ ἠλεημένοι νῦν δὲ ἐλεηθέντες.

verses.restored: Beloved, I appeal to you as sojourners and resident foreigners to abstain from fleshly desires that war against the soul/life,

familiar.text: Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul;

modern.text: Beloved, I urge you, as foreigners and exiles, to abstain from the desires of the flesh, which war against your soul.

original.text: Ἀγαπητοί, παρακαλῶ ὡς παροίκους καὶ παρεπιδήμους ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν σαρκικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν, αἵτινες στρατεύονται κατὰ τῆς ψυχῆς·

verses.restored: having your conduct beautiful among the nations, so that in what they speak against you as wrongdoers, from your beautiful works they may see and glorify the Divine in day of visitation.

familiar.text: Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.

modern.text: Conduct yourselves with such honor among the Gentiles that, though they slander you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day He visits us. Submission to Authorities (Romans 13:1–7)

original.text: τὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν ⸂ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἔχοντες καλήν⸃, ἵνα, ἐν ᾧ καταλαλοῦσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν, ἐκ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων ⸀ἐποπτεύοντες δοξάσωσι τὸν θεὸν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἐπισκοπῆς.

verses.restored: Be arranged under every human institution because of the Lord, whether to king as superior,

familiar.text: Submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake: whether it be to the king, as supreme;

modern.text: Submit yourselves for the Lord’s sake to every human institution, whether to the king as the supreme authority,

original.text: ⸀Ὑποτάγητε πάσῃ ἀνθρωπίνῃ κτίσει διὰ τὸν κύριον· εἴτε βασιλεῖ ὡς ὑπερέχοντι,

verses.restored: or to governors as sent through him for justice upon wrongdoers and praise of those doing good.

familiar.text: Or unto governors, as unto them that are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers, and for the praise of them that do well.

modern.text: or to governors as those sent by him to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right.

original.text: εἴτε ἡγεμόσιν ὡς διʼ αὐτοῦ πεμπομένοις εἰς ἐκδίκησιν κακοποιῶν ἔπαινον δὲ ἀγαθοποιῶν

verses.restored: For so is the will of the Divine, doing good to silence the ignorance of foolish humans.

familiar.text: For so is the will of God, that with well doing ye may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men:

modern.text: For it is God’s will that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish men.

original.text: (ὅτι οὕτως ἐστὶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀγαθοποιοῦντας φιμοῦν τὴν τῶν ἀφρόνων ἀνθρώπων ἀγνωσίαν)·

verses.restored: As free ones, and not having freedom as cover for harmfulness, but as servants of Divine.

familiar.text: As free, and not using your liberty for a cloke of maliciousness, but as the servants of God.

modern.text: Live in freedom, but do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil; live as servants of God.

original.text: ὡς ἐλεύθεροι, καὶ μὴ ὡς ἐπικάλυμμα ἔχοντες τῆς κακίας τὴν ἐλευθερίαν, ἀλλʼ ὡς ⸂θεοῦ δοῦλοι⸃.

verses.restored: Honor all. Love the siblinghood. Fear/revere the Divine. Honor the king.

familiar.text: Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king.

modern.text: Treat everyone with high regard: Love the brotherhood of believers, fear God, honor the king.

original.text: πάντας τιμήσατε, τὴν ἀδελφότητα ⸀ἀγαπᾶτε, τὸν θεὸν φοβεῖσθε, τὸν βασιλέα τιμᾶτε.

verses.restored: Household servants/enslaved ones, be arranged under masters with all reverence, not only the good and gentle but also the crooked.

familiar.text: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.

modern.text: Servants, submit yourselves to your masters with all respect, not only to those who are good and gentle, but even to those who are unreasonable.

original.text: Οἱ οἰκέται ὑποτασσόμενοι ἐν παντὶ φόβῳ τοῖς δεσπόταις, οὐ μόνον τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς καὶ ἐπιεικέσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς σκολιοῖς.

verses.restored: For this is grace, if because of consciousness of Divine someone endures griefs while suffering unjustly.

familiar.text: For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.

modern.text: For if anyone endures the pain of unjust suffering because he is conscious of God, this is to be commended.

original.text: τοῦτο γὰρ χάρις εἰ διὰ συνείδησιν θεοῦ ὑποφέρει τις λύπας πάσχων ἀδίκως·

verses.restored: For what credit if, sinning/misaligned and being struck, you endure? But if doing good and suffering you endure, this is grace before the Divine.

familiar.text: For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.

modern.text: How is it to your credit if you are beaten for doing wrong and you endure it? But if you suffer for doing good and you endure it, this is commendable before God. Christ’s Example of Suffering (Isaiah 53:1–8)

original.text: ποῖον γὰρ κλέος εἰ ἁμαρτάνοντες καὶ κολαφιζόμενοι ὑπομενεῖτε; ἀλλʼ εἰ ἀγαθοποιοῦντες καὶ πάσχοντες ὑπομενεῖτε, τοῦτο χάρις παρὰ θεῷ.

verses.restored: For into this you were called, because Messiah also suffered on behalf of you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow his tracks.

familiar.text: For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps:

modern.text: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in His footsteps:

original.text: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ἐκλήθητε, ὅτι καὶ Χριστὸς ἔπαθεν ὑπὲρ ⸀ὑμῶν, ὑμῖν ὑπολιμπάνων ὑπογραμμὸν ἵνα ἐπακολουθήσητε τοῖς ἴχνεσιν αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: He did no sin/misalignment, nor was deceit found in his mouth.

familiar.text: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth:

modern.text: “He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in His mouth.”

original.text: ὃς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: When reviled, he did not revile back; suffering, he did not threaten, but handed himself to the One judging justly.

familiar.text: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously:

modern.text: When they heaped abuse on Him, He did not retaliate; when He suffered, He made no threats, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly.

original.text: ὃς λοιδορούμενος οὐκ ἀντελοιδόρει, πάσχων οὐκ ἠπείλει, παρεδίδου δὲ τῷ κρίνοντι δικαίως·

verses.restored: He himself bore our sins/misalignments in his body upon the tree, so that, having died to sins/misalignments, we might live to righteousness/justice; by his wound you were healed.

familiar.text: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.

modern.text: He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. “By His stripes you are healed.”

original.text: ὃς τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν αὐτὸς ἀνήνεγκεν ἐν τῷ σώματι αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον, ἵνα ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ἀπογενόμενοι τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ ζήσωμεν· οὗ τῷ ⸀μώλωπι ἰάθητε.

verses.restored: For you were like sheep wandering, but now you turned back to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls/lives.

familiar.text: For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.

modern.text: For “you were like sheep going astray,” but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

original.text: ἦτε γὰρ ὡς πρόβατα ⸀πλανώμενοι, ἀλλὰ ἐπεστράφητε νῦν ἐπὶ τὸν ποιμένα καὶ ἐπίσκοπον τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν.

safety_note: 1 Peter 2:18-25 must not be used to sanctify slavery, workplace coercion, domestic abuse, or passive endurance of harm. The text addresses ancient household servants/enslaved people under unjust conditions and points to Messiah's non-retaliatory trust in Divine justice, not to enabling abusers. Reception-history audit required.
translation_notes: Living stones/royal priesthood language draws Israel Scripture imagery into a Messiah community and should not erase Jewish Israel.
Submission language is bounded by doing good, freedom, Divine service, and justice.
